claims.quote: QRS ≥ 120 ms Broad monomorphic R in I, V5, V6 (often notched) Deep S or QS pattern in V1

claims.text: Ischemia in LBBB: use the Sgarbossa criteria
claims.quote: consider Sgarbossa criteria for ischemia in LBBB

claims.text: Any concordant ST change is concerning for ischemia
claims.quote: Any concordant ST segment change is concerning for ischaemia.

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Mechanism: impulses go down the right bundle first, then reach the LV across the septum — septal activation reverses (no lateral Q waves)
claims.quote: In LBBB, conduction delay means that impulses travel first via the right bundle branch to the RV, and then to the LV via the septum Septal activation is thus reversed eliminating lateral Q waves

claims.text: Rarely occurs without organic heart disease
claims.quote: It is unusual for LBBB to exist in the absence of organic disease.

claims.text: Carries a higher risk of future cardiac events and death than RBBB
claims.quote: LBBB is associated with a structural heart disorder more often than is RBBB and, in contrast to RBBB, LBBB is associated with a higher risk of future cardiac events and mortality.

claims.text: Symptoms Rarely symptomatic itself, but LV dyssynchrony can reduce systolic function and contribute to heart failure
claims.quote: Isolated LBBB rarely produces symptoms but may produce interventricular mechanical dyssynchrony that reduces the efficiency of left ventricular systolic function and may contribute to heart failure

claims.text: Treatment Search for underlying heart disease
claims.quote: The presence of LBBB should prompt a search for underlying cardiac pathology

claims.text: With heart failure from reduced LV function: resynchronization pacing
claims.quote: particularly in association with other heart disorders that reduce left ventricular systolic function. Resynchronization pacing therapy is then of benefit

claims.text: Your EKG notes call a new LBBB with chest pain a STEMI equivalent.
claims.quote: new LBBB in the setting of chest pain is a STEMI equivalent

claims.text: LITFL notes this was once the teaching, but newer data show chest-pain patients with new LBBB have little added risk of acute MI; practice now looks for excessive discordance or concordant ST changes (Sgarbossa).
claims.quote: New LBBB in the context of chest pain was once considered a “STEMI-equivalent” and part of the criteria for thrombolysis. However, more up-to-date data suggests that chest pain patients with new LBBB have little increased risk of acute myocardial infarction at the time of presentation. Practice has now evolved to examining for excessive discordance or concordant ST segment changes indicative of infarction.
